Title: Intern | Artificial Intelligence (AI) | Bengaluru | TTC - DOMESTIC
SDE Intern
Description:
About Origin
Origin (previously 10xConstruction) is building general-purpose autonomous robots for US construction to tackle rising costs, safety risks, and labour shortages. Our modular, multi-trade platform combines purpose-built hardware with real-time site intelligence to navigate complex environments and execute tasks with precision. Trained in high-fidelity simulation and already deployed on live sites, our robots deliver 5x faster execution, 250%+ margin expansion, and significant cost savings. Join India’s most talent-dense robotics team consisting of individuals from IITs, Stanford, UCLA, etc.
About the Role
We're looking for an SDE Intern who can work across the stack — backend services, frontend dashboards, and the systems layer underneath. You'll build software that talks to real robots: telemetry pipelines, operator interfaces, APIs that bridge cloud and edge. Things break in interesting ways when your backend is running on a Jetson at a construction site, not just in a data centre. If you want to write code that ships to production and actually moves hardware, this is the role.
Responsibilities
Backend & APIs
Build and maintain backend services in Python — FastAPI, async workflows, background task processing.
Design and integrate REST and WebSocket APIs for robot telemetry, operator commands, and data ingestion.
Work with data processing pipelines that handle sensor data, image streams, and job-site logs.
Frontend
Develop frontend dashboards and operator tools using JavaScript and React.
Build interfaces that display real-time robot status, site data, and diagnostic information in a way that's actually useful to operators and engineers.
Iterate on UI based on feedback from the team and field deployments.
Systems & Infrastructure
Work on Linux-based systems — development, debugging, and deployments across cloud and edge (Jetson) environments.
Debug real production issues that cut across frontend, backend, and infrastructure. Trace a bug from a React component through an API to a misconfigured service on a device.
Help with containerised deployments using Docker, including building and maintaining images for multi-architecture targets.
Understand how processes, networking, and file systems behave on the machines your code runs on — not just the application layer.
Collaboration
Work closely with robotics and systems engineers to support robot workflows and integrate software with hardware pipelines.
Contribute to internal tooling, developer documentation, and shared libraries
Requirements
Strong fundamentals in computer science — data structures, algorithms, and systems thinking.
Proficiency in Python. You can write clean, maintainable code, not just scripts that work once.
Working knowledge of JavaScript and React — enough to build and modify frontend components.
Comfortable on Linux: CLI, processes, permissions, basic networking. You don't panic when you need to SSH into a box and figure out why something isn't running.
Understanding of APIs, client-server architecture, and async patterns.
Ability to read, understand, and modify existing codebases — not just greenfield work.
Good to have -
Specialization in React — deeper experience with state management, component architecture, hooks, performance optimization, and building complex interactive UIs beyond basic CRUD dashboards.
Specialization in Android — experience building native Android apps (Kotlin/Java), working with Android lifecycle, background services, and sensor/hardware APIs. Relevant for field-facing mobile tools used on construction sites.
Experience with Docker and containers — writing Dockerfiles, debugging container issues, understanding image layers.
Basic DevOps knowledge: CI/CD pipelines, deployment workflows, monitoring and logging.
Familiarity with databases — PostgreSQL, SQLite, or similar. Understanding of schema design and query optimisation basics.
Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS / GCP).
Understanding of networking basics: TCP/UDP, DNS, ports, firewalls — helpful when debugging why your service can't talk to the robot.
Interest in robotics, real-time systems, edge computing, or distributed systems
Internship Details -
This is a six-month contract-to-hire position, with strong potential for longer-term opportunities depending on your contributions and interests. You'll work alongside a small, high-calibre team shipping real autonomy infrastructure — not toy projects. If you want to learn fast and see your work running on robots deployed on live construction sites, this is the role.
Benefits
Gain experience in a dynamic startup environment at the forefront of robotics and AI innovation.
Contribute to the development of technology that will revolutionize the construction industry.
Work alongside a talented and passionate team committed to making a real-world impact.
Learn from experienced professionals and gain valuable skills in robotics software engineering.
Gain practical experience in a real-world engineering environment.
Contribute to a project with the potential to make a significant impact on the construction industry.

Title: AI-GTM Engineer
Description:
About Signeasy
Contracts run businesses. We are unlocking the intelligence inside them.
Signeasy began fifteen years ago with a simple idea. Signing should be easy. That idea helped the world go paperless.
But signatures were only the beginning.
Today, the real problem isn’t signing contracts. It’s what happens after.
Across every company, contracts sit scattered across inboxes, shared drives, CLMs, ERPs, and filing systems. They’re static. Forgotten. Underused. And yet, they quietly define revenue, risk, compliance, and growth.
We believe contracts are one of the most powerful and most overlooked sources of truth in a business.
2025 changed everything. While others continued to treat contracts as mere paperwork, we transformed Signeasy into an intelligent, AI‑powered contract management platform – turning static contracts into living, searchable, and insight‑rich systems of record. We shipped major product improvements, achieved key compliance milestones, were featured at Apple’s WWDC, and laid the foundation for what comes next.
2026 will be our biggest year yet. With Intelligent Contract Management as the next chapter of Signeasy, we’re going to market with an AI‑powered contract management platform built for modern teams who expect more than storage, signatures, or status‑quo software.
This is the moment. And this is the team building it. If you want to help shape the future of contracts with us, please read on.
About the Role
As our AI GTM Operations Engineer, you won’t just maintain systems – you’ll design them. You’ll be responsible for building an AI‑first GTM engine around Signeasy: how data flows, how signals are captured, how decisions get made, and how we convert insight into revenue.
You’ll work at the intersection of RevOps, AI, and GTM strategy, building the infrastructure, workflows, dashboards, and outbound lists that help Marketing, Sales, and CS move faster, focus on the right accounts, and win more often.
Your work will directly influence:
How we define and measure revenue outcomes (trialpaid, pipeline velocity, churn, expansion)
How our GTM systems across Signeasy are architected, automated, and scaled
How AI agents, scoring models, dashboards, and outbound lists show up in the daily lives of GTM teams
As we scale, there’s a clear growth path into leading GTM Operations or broader Revenue Operations.
What you’ll do
Design and own AI‑first GTM systems
Architect and own GTM systems across HubSpot, Apollo, ChurnZero, Clay, and related tools.
Turn business goals (conversion, velocity, churn) into concrete workflows, rules, experiments, and dashboards.
Build “always‑on” systems where signals, scoring, routing, and alerts happen automatically, not in spreadsheets.
Build and maintain clear GTM dashboards and scorecards so leaders can quickly see performance across trials, pipeline, churn, and expansion.
Build the revenue data, CRM, and outbound backbone
Own HubSpot data architecture, lifecycle stages, and governance as the core GTM database.
Ensure clean, consistent data across Marketing, Sales, and CS – from first touch to renewal.
Design and maintain segmentation and audience frameworks that power campaigns, outbound, and lifecycle programs.
Use tools like Clay and Apollo to build dynamic, AI‑enriched outbound account and contact lists based on ICP, firmographics, technographics, intent, contract triggers, and performance feedback.
Turn AI from assistive to decisive
Implement AI‑driven lead, account, and health scoring based on intent, product usage, and contract signals.
Design workflows where AI doesn’t just enrich data, but recommends next best actions for Sales and CS in the tools they live in.
Partner with GTM leaders to define what “good” looks like for predictive models (conversion, churn, expansion) and continuously improve them.
Elevate CS and customer health
Evolve health scoring beyond basic usage into richer, contract‑aware signals (renewals, terms, risk, expansion triggers).
Give CSMs a daily, prioritized view of where to act, why now, and how.
Make customer health and expansion opportunities visible across the full GTM org.
Run experiments, not just reports
Define hypotheses, success metrics, and iteration plans for trial scoring, outbound programs, and lifecycle journeys.
Instrument experiments end‑to‑end and close the loop with clear learnings and decisions.
Build a culture where systems, not opinions, decide what gets scaled.
Protect focus and automate the rest
Handle BAU GTM ops requests with clear expectations and SLAs, while protecting time for strategic work.
Use AI agents and lightweight automations (and when relevant, interns) to offload low‑stakes, repetitive tasks like enrichment, dedupe, list maintenance, and report prep.
Document systems, create playbooks, and enable teams to self‑serve wherever possible.
AI‑first expectations (Non‑Negotiable)
All roles at Signeasy explicitly require an AI‑first way of working, and this role is no exception.
As an AI GTM Operations Manager, you are expected to actively use, experiment with, and design AI‑powered workflows in your daily work.
You should have experience with (or strong curiosity toward):
AI for GTM data, enrichment, and lists
Using tools like Clay, Apollo, Clearbit, ZoomInfo, or similar.
Building dynamic, enriched outbound lists based on ICP, firmographics, technographics, intent, and contract‑relevant triggers.
AI for scoring, routing, and prioritization
Designing or operating AI‑assisted lead, account, and health scoring models.
Building workflows that turn signals (product usage, lifecycle events, contract milestones) into who to talk to, about what, and when.
AI for reporting and decision support
Automating recurring dashboards, scorecards, and reporting wherever possible, ensuring stakeholders have reliable self‑serve views instead of ad‑hoc asks.
Surfacing dynamic, context‑aware views for GTM teams (e.g., “this week’s at‑risk accounts”, “top expansion opportunities”, “trial cohorts off‑track”).
AI agents & workflow thinking
Experimenting with or building lightweight workflow agents that orchestrate multiple tools.
Thinking in terms of systems and leverage: signal enrichment scoring routing alerts action.
If the phrase “I automated that” excites you more than “I updated that manually”, you’ll feel at home here.
What we’re looking for
3–6 years in Revenue Operations, GTM Operations, Marketing/Sales/CS Ops, or CRM Operations (B2B SaaS strongly preferred).
Strong hands‑on experience with HubSpot (objects, workflows, reporting, and integrations).
Experience managing and integrating GTM tools such as HubSpot, Apollo, ChurnZero, Clay, or similar.
Solid understanding of SaaS funnels, lifecycle stages, and revenue metrics.
Demonstrated use of AI in GTM workflows (or clear proof that you learn and adopt new tools fast).
A systems mindset: you see processes, edge cases, and failure modes before they break.
Clear, concise communication with the ability to translate complexity into simple, actionable views.
Why this role is special
You’ll help define how an AI‑first GTM engine around Signeasy works, not just plug into an old one.
You’ll work on a product and category with real differentiation and momentum in AI‑powered contract management.
You’ll operate with high ownership and visibility across leadership, Product, Marketing, Sales, and CS.
You’ll build skills at the frontier of AI‑native RevOps, dashboards, and outbound GTM automation.
You’ll have a clear path to broader Revenue Operations leadership as we scale.

Title: Software Engineer II - Pear Assessment
Description:
What We Do
At GoGuardian, we're helping build a future where all learners are ready and inspired to solve the world's greatest challenges. Our award-winning system of learning solutions is purpose-built for K-12 and trusted by school leaders to promote effective teaching and equitable engagement while helping empower educators to keep students safe.
What It's Like to Work at GoGuardian
We are an outcomes-focused learning company with a steadfast focus on improving learning environments, one classroom at a time. Working with us means joining a remote team of diverse, committed, mission-driven employees who are inspired by our vision, dedicated to our customers, and ready to roll up their sleeves. Guardians put their heads together to solve problems, learn together from experiments that fail, and stand together by their work with full accountability. We balance our diligence with an inclusive culture that invites everyone to bring their whole self to work. Join us and learn why "I love the people here" is one of the most frequent comments we hear from Guardians.
The Role
We're looking for a
Software Engineer II, Fullstack
to design and implement solid architectural solutions with the rest of the engineering team, supporting our Pear Assessment product - a platform that provides real-time, interactive formative assessments, enabling teachers to capture diverse student responses, gain instant insights, and adapt instruction across live and self-paced learning environments.
With a passion for solving problems quickly and delivering high-quality code, you will build features that enable real-time formative assessments and actionable learning insights for educators. You'll work across the full stack—from crafting intuitive React-based classroom experiences and interactive assessment workflows to designing scalable backend services and optimizing data pipelines that power instant feedback and analytics. You will also contribute to OpenSearch-powered semantic search capabilities, enabling fast and relevant discovery across more than 500 million educational documents. Our Engineering team thrives on a purpose-driven culture of collaboration, openness, trust, and transparency, with individuals who continuously push boundaries to improve teaching and learning outcomes.
What You'll Do
Design, build, and continually improve our Pear Assessment product and related services
Build and ship features that power real-time formative assessments and classroom engagement experiences for educators and students.
Develop & maintain high-performance backend services in Typescript that power the assessment platform
Develop intuitive, high-performance React interfaces for interactive assessments, dashboards, and data visualization
Develop and enhance OpenSearch-based semantic search systems to enable fast, relevant discovery across hundreds of millions of educational documents
Optimize data pipelines and queries to deliver low-latency insights and feedback to teachers during live and asynchronous sessions
Collaborate cross-functionally with product, design, and data teams to translate educational needs into impactful technical solutions.
Ensure system reliability, scalability, and performance under high usage across classrooms and districts.
Continuously improve code quality, testing practices, and engineering standards within a collaborative team environment.
Participate in architecture discussions, code reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives
Architect and operate cloud-native systems on AWS, leveraging services like SQS for asynchronous processing and event-driven workflows.
Work with MongoDB and other data stores to model, store, and efficiently query large-scale assessment and engagement data.
Integrate AWS IoT services where applicable to support real-time classroom device interactions and data ingestion.
Integrate LLM/AI services to power intelligent features such as automated insights, content generation, and enhanced search relevance.
Who You Are
4+ years of professional industry experience building and delivering scalable software features in a production environment
